Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

either adjective and pronoun

one or the other of two

also either one, either of you, either of them, whichever of the two, on either side

classical

Ter. And. 10: quī utramvīs rēctē nōrit, ambās nōverit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Sen. 33: minus habeō vīrium quam vestrum utervīs (Lewis & Short)

utervīs, utravīs, utrumvīs

pronoun and adjective; uter declines, -vīs stays

either of two, whichever you like

Either one, it does not matter which (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • alteruter, alterutra, alterutrum — one or the other (one of the two, whichever it is)

    pronoun and adjective; also written apart, altera utra, alterum utrum · also used · classical · Cic. Div. Caec. 18: videō esse necesse alterutrum (Lewis & Short)

    One of the two must be so, though it is not said which.

  • uterque, utraque, utrumque — either (= each) of two: on either side

    pronoun and adjective · also used · classical · Gell. 3.10.12: ex utrāque parte

    English “on either side” means on both: ex utrāque parte (see both). “Not … either” is neuter (see neither).

Examples

  • tange utramvīs digitulō minimō modo

    just touch either of them with your little fingerPlaut. Rud. 3.4.15 (Lewis & Short)

  • at minus habeō vīrium quam vestrum utervīs

    but I have less strength than either of youCic. Sen. 33 (Lewis & Short)

  • in aurem utramvīs ōtiōsē dormīre

    to sleep soundly on either ear (without a care)Ter. Heaut. 342 (Lewis & Short, Heaut. 2.3.101)

  • dentēs quoque et in septem mēnsibus prīmīs et septēnōs ex utrāque parte gignī ait et cadere annīs septimīs

    he says that the teeth, too, come through in the first seven months, seven on either side, and fall out in the seventh yearGell. 3.10.12

  • videō esse necesse alterutrum

    I see that one or the other must be soCic. Div. Caec. 18 (Lewis & Short)

See also both, neither.
